newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan king to meet Mobutu over Zaire developments.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan king to meet Mobutu over Zaire developments.

text.p: Morocco's King Hassan and Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko will meet late on Wednesday to discuss the latest events in Zaire, shaken by a rebel advance.
"His Majesty King Hassan will receive President Mobutu tonight around 9 p.m (2100 GMT) at the royal palace of Rabat," a senior Moroccan official, who declined to be named, said.
"The two head of states are expected to discuss bilateral relations and the latest developments in Zaire," he added without elaborating.
The Zairean leader arrived in Morocco on Monday for a three-day working visit on his way to Zaire from France where he has been convalescing from prostate cancer surgery.

Officials at the Moroccan foreign ministry declined to comment on a possibility of Morocco sending troops to Kinshasa to back the Zairean army against rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).
Rebels have extended their push into Zaire's mineral- producing Shaba province, after countering the army's much-trumpeted offensive by opening a new front, sources on both sides say.
Moroccan troops in 1977 took part in putting down a secessionist uprising in the southern province of Shaba after Zairean forces failed to make any headway.
The royal armed forces also relieved French and Belgian paratroops giving support to the Zairean authorities in the mining town of Kolwezi the following year.
Since undergoing prostate surgery in Switzerland on August 22, Mobutu has spent most of his time in his palatial French Riviera residence at Roquebrune-Cap Martin.

He returned briefly to Zaire in December and ordered an army reorganisation to launch a counter-offensive against the rebels near the border with Rwanda and Uganda, but flew back to France last month for further medical checks.
Mobutu is expected to leave Morocco for Kinshasa on Thursday at 7 a.m (0700 GMT), a Moroccan official said.
